bugs: ProcessWebhookEvent::failed() (app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:77-80) calls markFailed with no status guard, so a late failed() (e.g. a timeout after the transaction has committed) flips a Processed event back to Failed. A probe confirmed this.
VerifyWebhookSignature (app/Http/Middleware/VerifyWebhookSignature.php:18) compares the hex digest case-sensitively, so a provider that sends uppercase hex gets a 401. A probe confirmed this. Minor.
StoreWebhookEventRequest: 'data' => required|array returns 422 for an event with an empty data object {}. Minor, and impl-2 shares it.
Only the validated keys are stored as the payload (ReceiveWebhookController.php:16), so any extra top-level fields in the provider event are dropped.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:106 uses `markPaid(...) && $order->user->notify(...)` as a short-circuit side effect inside a match arm. notify() returns void, so this is too clever by half.
app/Console/Commands/RedispatchStuckWebhookEvents.php plus the scheduler entry add a stuck-event sweeper the task did not ask for. It is extra ceremony, though defensible.
app/Models/Order.php:46 json_encodes payment_details by hand in a raw query update while the model also casts that column as array. That is inconsistent.
tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:181 asserts the backoff by reading the Backoff attribute via Reflection, which tests configuration rather than behaviour.
app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:58 markProcessing() is a no-op save on retries, so updated_at goes stale. That couples badly with the stuck sweeper.
strengths: Uses modern job attributes: #[Backoff], #[MaxExceptions] and #[Timeout] together with retryUntil, WithoutOverlapping with releaseAfter/expireAfter, and RateLimited backed by RateLimiter::for(perSecond(10)).

Treats errors precisely: 5xx and connection errors are rethrown for retry, 429 is released honouring Retry-After, and 4xx, validation errors and a missing order go to fail(). failed() records the error.
createOrFirst on a unique event_id plus wasRecentlyCreated gives race-safe once-only storage and dispatch.
Conditional status-transition updates stop out-of-order events from downgrading an order and stop a second receipt from being sent. Refunds are idempotent on provider_refund_id.
The receipt is a queued notification implementing ShouldQueueAfterCommit and is sent inside the transaction.
Thin invokable controller, form requests with typed accessors, an API resource, and policy gating via ->can().
Retrying a failed event with queue:retry works. A probe confirmed it.
Thorough README on deployment: Supervisor, shared cache, retry_after versus timeout, queue:restart, and the scheduler.
Behavioural rate-limiter test (12 jobs: 10 pass, 2 released), plus an end-to-end HTTP-to-queue test.

bugs: WebhookEvent::claim() (app/Models/WebhookEvent.php:45-55) only accepts the Pending and Processing statuses, so once an event is marked Failed, running `queue:retry` on its job silently returns without processing it. A probe confirmed this. Failed events cannot be recovered.

ProcessWebhookEvent.php:80 reads `(int) $details['amount']` without a default. If the provider response has no amount, PHP raises an 'Undefined array key' error, which is retried as a transient exception up to MaxExceptions times. A probe confirmed this.

Order::markPaid (app/Models/Order.php:43) overwrites the order's amount and currency with the provider's values, and sets currency to null when the provider omits it. A probe confirmed the order's currency was wiped. This corrupts order data and was not requested.
Order::refund (app/Models/Order.php:59) uses an unconditional update to Refunded, which is inconsistent with the guarded transitions used for the other statuses.
Uppercase signatures are accepted but empty data objects get a 422 (same as impl-1). Minor.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/ProcessWebhookEvent.php:80-81 uses the same `markPaid(...) && notify(...)` side-effect trick inside a match arm.
app/Models/WebhookEvent.php:14 and app/Models/Order.php:13 make status, error and processed_at mass-assignable.
bootstrap/app.php:20 adds an unnecessary redirectGuestsTo pointing at a nonexistent 'login' route for non-API requests.
tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:153 calls $job->failed() by hand with a fabricated exception rather than asserting what the real failure path records.
tests/Feature/ProcessWebhookEventTest.php:187-191 tests the rate limit only by inspecting the Limit configuration, not the RateLimited middleware's behaviour.
No failed_at column, so the time of failure is not visible.
strengths: The same solid queue toolkit: #[Backoff], #[MaxExceptions], #[Timeout] and #[DeleteWhenMissingModels] attributes, retryUntil, WithoutOverlapping keyed on event_id, and RateLimited with perSecond(10).
markFailed() refuses to overwrite a Processed event (and this is tested).
Stricter ingestion validation with required_if rules per event type.
The receipt notification uses ShouldQueueAfterCommit with its own #[Tries] and #[Backoff]; SendQueuedNotifications in the installed version reads both attributes.
Looks up the order before calling the API, which saves rate-limit budget for orphaned events.
Daily model:prune with onOneServer, and a concise, accurate README on deployment.
Admin tests use real HTTP Basic credentials, and there is a 5xx-then-success retry test.

v.rationale:
Both implementations are built almost the same way: an invokable controller with createOrFirst, signature middleware, a job using the Backoff/MaxExceptions/Timeout attributes with retryUntil, WithoutOverlapping and RateLimited, conditional status transitions, a ShouldQueueAfterCommit receipt, and MassPrunable with model:prune. All tests pass in both (impl-1: 42, impl-2: 37). The probes are what separate them.

impl-2 has three real correctness bugs:
- **Failed events cannot be retried.** claim() rejects the Failed status, so running `queue:retry` on the job does nothing.
- **A missing provider field is retried as if it were transient.** If the provider response has no amount, the job hits an undefined-array-key error and retries it.
- **Order data gets overwritten.** markPaid replaces the order's amount and currency with provider data, and sets currency to null when the provider omits it.

impl-1's problems are smaller:
- failed() can flip a Processed event to Failed if it runs late.
- Signature comparison is case-sensitive, so uppercase hex is rejected.
- It adds a stuck-event sweeper the task didn't ask for, which is some extra ceremony.

impl-1 also has better tests. Its rate-limiter test exercises the middleware's behaviour (12 jobs, 10 pass, 2 released), and it includes an end-to-end HTTP-to-queue test.

impl-2 has stricter ingestion validation and a guarded markFailed. Those strengths don't outweigh its bugs, so impl-1 ranks first.
